description: Machine-readable registry of the 26 architecture tests (docs/testing/architecture-tests.md) plus the canary-purity test. Read by scripts/checks/architecture.mjs, which enforces the activation gate: a test whose activationPhase has been reached without an implementation fails the run.

statusValues.ACTIVE: The guarded structure exists now; the check runs on every invocation and must pass.
statusValues.NOT_APPLICABLE_UNTIL_PHASE_X: The guarded structure does not exist yet. activationPhase names the phase at which the structure arrives; from that phase on, an unimplemented check fails the run.

tests.name: Domain purity
tests.notes: Real target today: the four pure packages have source. modules/*/domain/ is scanned too and passes vacuously (no .ts yet); non-vacuousness is proven by the built-in self-test on every run.

tests.name: Layer direction
tests.notes: Modules have no code yet; the scan runs against the real glob and passes vacuously today. The self-test seeds a domain->infrastructure import and asserts the check fails on it.

tests.name: Module boundary
tests.notes: Cross-module imports must target public-api.ts only. Vacuous today (no module code); self-test seeds a bypass and asserts failure.

tests.name: No ORM leakage
tests.notes: prisma/@prisma imports allowed only under infrastructure/persistence/ paths. Scans apps, packages, and modules source.

tests.name: Ports declared inward
tests.notes: Activated in Phase 2 with the first real adapter (modules/audit/infrastructure). Every adapter-suffixed class (Adapter/Writer/Repository/Provider/Store/Gateway/Client/Publisher/Consumer/Relay/Source/Sink) exported from modules/*/infrastructure must implement an interface declared under that module's application/ports/. Self-test seeds an adapter without a port and asserts failure.

tests.name: No business logic in controllers
tests.notes: Activated in Phase 2. Declared complexity budget for *controller* files in apps/*/src and modules/*/presentation: max 8 route-decorator handlers, max 250 lines, and no import of any module's domain/ (directly or via @karar/<module>/domain) — domain access goes through a use case. Self-test seeds a fat controller importing domain and asserts failure on both rules.

tests.name: Money discipline
tests.notes: Monetary positions exist now (shared-kernel Money/Percentage/ExchangeRate, financial-engine zero()). Lexical check: monetary-named fields typed as number, and parseFloat/toFixed, in pure packages and module domain/application source. Type-level enforcement deepens with the engine in Phase 2/6.

tests.name: Event catalogue - published events
tests.notes: The catalogue file exists with zero events, so the structural check can and does run: the catalogue must parse, every entry must be well-formed, every DomainEvent implementation in code must be catalogued, and publish call sites with an empty catalogue fail. Today it verifies the catalogue parses and no event definitions exist outside it. Consumer-side allowedConsumers enforcement deepens when the bus exists (Phase 2). Coordination note (Phase 2, workstreams D/F): the checker validates the minimal required shape and ignores unknown fields, so D's richer catalogue entries (envelope/version/retention additions) extend entries without changes here; payload-rule constraints (test 15) stay as specified.

tests.name: Tenant scoping
tests.notes: Activated in Phase 3 with the first tenant-scoped repositories. Principal-scoped tables are derived from the canonical migrations (ENABLE+FORCE and not on rls-allow-list.json) and mapped to Prisma delegates via the schema's @@map; every modules/*/infrastructure/persistence file querying such a delegate must have principal context in reach — withPrincipalContext/withTenant, a transaction-local set_config('app.*', …, true) bind, or an import of a same-module persistence binder that has one (the IdentityPrismaScope pattern). The same check enforces SET LOCAL discipline everywhere: set_config('app.*', …, false) and session-level SET app.* fail. Self-test seeds an unscoped principal-delegate query and a session-scoped bind (and asserts the transaction-local binder shape is NOT flagged). Runtime enforcement is layered: withPrincipalContext fails closed on missing keys, and the adversarial suites (modules/*/__tests__, tests/security) prove the RLS boundary on live PostgreSQL.

tests.name: No direct provider access
tests.notes: Forbidden cloud SDK specifiers, provider URI/resource-name literals (gs://, arn:aws, projects/<id>/...), and provider env-var names, outside infrastructure/providers/ and infrastructure/persistence/.

tests.name: Deterministic domain
tests.notes: Real target today: financial-engine and the other pure packages. Forbids system clock reads and random sources in modules/*/domain/ and the four pure packages.

tests.name: No jurisdiction branching
tests.notes: Lexical check: conditionals and switches on jurisdiction/country identifiers in modules/*/{domain,application,presentation}. Vacuous today; self-test proves it fails on a seeded countryCode comparison. Localization/reference-data exemptions live outside these layers by construction.

tests.name: Sealed containment
tests.activationCriterion: sealed-vault module code exists (Documents + Sealed Vault phase). The static SEALED-content scan is part of this test and activates with it; today no code carries SEALED-marked content to scan.

tests.name: Grant required
tests.activationCriterion: SealedRecordStore and SealAccessGrant types exist; vault transaction isolation is implementable and checkable.

tests.name: Event catalogue - payload rules
tests.notes: Shares the catalogue checker with test 8. The payload-rule constraints (SEALED events identifier-only; HIGHLY_SENSITIVE_FINANCIAL payload requires a declared payloadExemption with owner, reason, reviewer) are enforced against every catalogue entry; with zero entries the constraint set runs against an empty list and the catalogue's shape is still verified.

tests.name: Pure packages
tests.notes: The four pure packages carry no runtime dependencies except @karar/shared-kernel where documented; shared-kernel itself carries none. devDependencies are allowed.

tests.name: Storage access
tests.notes: Object-storage client imports (minio, @google-cloud/storage, @aws-sdk/client-s3) only inside modules/documents/infrastructure/ or infrastructure/providers/. Vacuous today; real scan, self-tested.

tests.name: Approval policy
tests.activationCriterion: PolicyPack qa/v1 and the capability registry with disclosure declarations exist; ApprovalPolicy entries become checkable in packs.

tests.name: Kernel surface
tests.notes: packages/shared-kernel/src/index.ts must export exactly the nine universals: Money, Currency, Percentage, ExchangeRate, Clock, Result, DomainEvent, TenantId, UserId. Any tenth export, or a missing one, fails.

tests.name: Pinning
tests.notes: Activated in Phase 3 with the first legal-consequence tables. The declared set (LEGAL_CONSEQUENCE_TABLES in the checker: consent_grants and data_protection_role_assignments) is verified against the REAL canonical migrations: each of the four pinning dimensions (data-model.md §5) maps to the actual NOT NULL column that carries it — jurisdiction_ref and operating_entity_id in Phase 3, per migration 0063's recorded interpretation — or declares a deferral to the phase whose machinery introduces the value (policyPackVersionAtCreation and subjectPolicySelectionVersion: 3.5, when PolicyPacks and SubjectPolicySelection exist). A deferral whose phase has arrived fails the run, exactly like this registry's activation gate; no dimension is ever satisfied by a fabricated value. Undeclared tables carrying the pinning signature (*_at_creation columns or a per-row operating_entity_id) fail. Self-test seeds a declared table missing its jurisdiction pin, an undeclared *_at_creation table, and a due deferral (fixture currentPhase 4).

tests.name: RLS coverage
tests.notes: Activated in Phase 3 with the first tenant-scoped tables. Parses every canonical migration (packages/platform/db/migrations/*.sql — the schema of record): each created table is either ENABLE + FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with at least one policy, or carried on packages/platform/db/rls-allow-list.json with table, reason, owner, compensatingGrants, and reviewPhase all non-empty. All three failure shapes detect: no RLS, enabled-without-policy, and FORCEd-without-enabled (the legacy audit table's own anomaly, RLS-01/RLS-02/P14). A stale allow-list entry naming a table no migration creates also fails. Live-database verification of the same facts is db:verify plus the adversarial suites (modules/*/__tests__, tests/security), which probe the policies as karar_app and the owner on real rows. Self-test seeds all three shapes, a stale entry, and an empty reason field.

tests.name: No declared guard without call site
tests.notes: Activated in Phase 2 with the first guard class (audit's AuditMetadataGuard; config guards count as they land). Every class named *Guard in apps/*/src, packages/*/src, or modules/** must be referenced from non-test code outside its own declaration; tests do not count as call sites. Self-test seeds an unreferenced FooGuard and asserts failure.

tests.name: Resource limits declared
tests.activationCriterion: First ingestion path (manual/CSV) or rendering path exists; explicit byte/row/page/wall-clock/memory limits become declarable and checkable.

tests.name: Lifecycle declarations
tests.notes: Deepened in Phase 2 with the first real schema (audit.audit_events): a module with implementation code must declare the full six-field table (subject relationship, purpose, classification, retention, export treatment, erasure strategy), and six-field tables are validated field by field — canonical subject/classification/erasure values, export treatment included|excluded (reason)|n/a with 'excluded' requiring a stated reason, and placeholders (TBD/TODO/empty) forbidden. Skeleton modules without code keep the erasure-only obligation. Also parses packages/platform/db/DATA_LIFECYCLE.md (platform-owned tables: schema_migrations now; workstream D appends outbox/jobs rows) with the same six-field rules. Self-test seeds a non-canonical strategy, a code-bearing module without the six-field table, and a placeholder row.

tests.name: Assurance-claim traceability
tests.notes: Referential integrity of docs/security/assurance-claims.md: every AC-### row has non-empty evidence and owner; statuses limited to VERIFIED/PENDING/UNVERIFIED; every 'test N' evidence reference exists in this registry; and this registry contains all 26 canonical tests.

tests.name: Canary purity
tests.activationCriterion: The sealed-integrity canary is designed and implemented (key custody strategy phase); its plaintext becomes inspectable for customer-derived content.
